newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices ease as govt stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices ease as govt stocks rise.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Wednesday eased on reports of a rise in stocks held by government agencies, dealers said.
Mill buying was sluggish while stockists turned active sellers on reports of rising inventories with the state-owned agencies.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by five rupees at 865/920 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned fell by 15/30 rupees at 1,510/1,640 rupees per maund.
Cotton F-414 fell by 30/40 rupees at 1,880/1,900 rupees per maund while Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) eased by 200/300 rupees at 12,700/13,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
"Some state-owned agencies are witnessing a glut of cotton due to lower offtake and higher procurement and these agencies may cut selling prices to reduce inventories," one broker said.
